name: Diagnose-a-Drop Framework
subtitle: When CPL jumps or ROAS falls suddenly
steps: 1. Tracking: Is the Pixel, CAPI, or Lead Form working? Any broken links?
2. Audience: Did Frequency jump > 3.5? Is there audience fatigue or overlap?
3. Creative: Have CTR and hook watch-time dropped over the last 3 days?
4. Offer / Landing: Is the website slow (> 3s)? Did checkout pricing change?
5. Budget / Bids: Did a sudden budget edit reset the machine learning phase?
6. Outside Factors: Festive holiday, competitor sale, or public event?
pixieTip: Always compare CPM, CTR, and CVR side-by-side to pinpoint exactly where the break happened.

name: The 8-Step Launch Plan
subtitle: How to structure a new client or product campaign
steps: 1. Business Goal: Clear revenue or lead target (e.g., 50 bookings/month at ₹100 CPL)
2. Audience: Balanced local or broad targeting with ideal customer demographics
3. Irresistible Offer: Hook with value (free trial, bundle, or consultation)
4. Creative Mix: 2-3 vertical videos (UGC/Reel) + 1 high-contrast carousel
5. Starting Budget: 3x to 5x target CPL daily
6. Tracking Setup: Pixel + CAPI tested with Google Tag Manager or native partner
7. Review Dates: Day 1 (Delivery), Day 3 (CTR), Day 7 (CPL/ROAS)
8. Scaling Plan: Increase budget 15-20% on winning ad sets only
pixieTip: Keep campaigns consolidated. Having 20 tiny ad sets starves the machine learning algorithm.

name: Client-Talk Formula
subtitle: How to explain performance to non-technical stakeholders
steps: 1. What Happened: State the core number simply ('We generated 42 leads this week at ₹95 each')
2. Why: Explain in plain terms ('Our customer testimonial Reel achieved a 2.4% CTR')
3. What I Did / Will Do: Concrete next actions ('I am scaling the winning ad set by 20%')
4. What I Need From You: Any approvals or customer feedback needed
5. Next Update: Clear date and time for the next report
pixieTip: Never dump acronyms like CPM and EMQ on a business owner without explaining what they mean in Rupees.

name: The 4-Part Metric Answer Formula
subtitle: How to answer any metric question in an interview
steps: 1. Definition: What the metric is in one plain sentence
2. Formula: How it is mathematically calculated
3. Why it matters: What business signal it reveals
4. Action: What you would physically DO in Ads Manager if it is too high or low
pixieTip: Interviewers love candidates who connect numbers to physical optimization actions!
